rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Table 2-4 <U+2013> two-year outdoor pot trial (1998-1999) on autumn-sown sugar beet with three drip-irrigation frequencies (SWD1-3), TDR soil moisture monitoring and root length density at harvest.
rows.notes: The study does not measure root-zone water tension (matric potential) and reports no -10 to -30 kPa range; it measures volumetric soil water content by TDR. Its own data (Figure 3a) show that soil moisture before irrigation was close to wilting point in the top 0.2 m for all treatments and diverged strongly in deeper layers (21.8-18.7% for SWD2-3 vs near field capacity for SWD1), i.e. root-zone water status was not stable across irrigation intervals. What the study does show is that total daily root water uptake (1471 vs 1440-1410 mL/day) did not differ significantly among the three drip frequencies, which the authors attribute to root acclimation (uptake shifting to deeper layers, higher root/shoot ratio), not to stable water tension. All treatments were drip, so there is no comparison of drip against another method. The effect named in the passage (stable root-zone tension buffering interval effects) is therefore not a result of this study; Q2 answered no.

notes: Full text available and complete. Pot experiment (single plant per 1.3 m PVC pot, four replications, one soil, one site, two years); results are reported with standard errors (Tables 3-4) but this is not relevant since Q2 is no.
